findings.measured: True peak is +2.8 dBTP, above full scale; expect distortion on playback and after lossy encoding.

steps.text: Put Limiter last on the Main track with Ceiling at −1.0 dB and True Peak on (Live 12; on older versions use −1.5 dB).

other_options.text: Before bouncing, play the whole song through a loudness meter and check integrated LUFS and true peak.

findings.measured: 4.4 dB lighter below 100 Hz than your reference, at matched volume.

steps.text: Put EQ Eight on the Main track and use a low shelf over the lows (below 100 Hz), boosting about 4.5 dB.

other_options.text: Loop the loudest section and switch between your master and the reference, at matched volume, while you set the boost.

findings.measured: Loudness is -2.7 LUFS; typical for Trap / hip-hop is -9 to -6 LUFS.

steps.text: Lower Limiter's Gain by 2–4 dB and compare at matched volume.

findings.measured: Punch is 5.5 dB PLR; typical for Trap / hip-hop is 6 to 9.5 dB PLR.

steps.text: Lower Limiter's Gain by 2–4 dB and compare at matched volume.

other_options.text: On the drum bus, use a compressor with a slower attack (10–30 ms) or a transient shaper to bring back punch.

notes.headline: This master is clipping hard — +2.8 dBTP true peak and -2.68 LUFS — so pulling the limiter back is the first and biggest fix.
notes.summary: Your balance and stereo picture are in good shape, and you're at 97% match to your reference, but the level is the problem: true peak reads +2.8 dBTP, above full scale, which will distort on playback and after lossy encoding. Integrated loudness is -2.68 LUFS where Trap / hip-hop typically sits at -9 to -6 LUFS, and that push is also why punch measures 5.5 dB PLR against a typical 6 to 9.5 dB. Backing the limiter off fixes all three at once. After that, the one tone note is that you're 4.4 dB lighter below 100 Hz than your reference at matched volume.

priorities.title: Pull the limiter back and catch the true peaks
priorities.why: At +2.8 dBTP the file is over full scale — converters and MP3/AAC encoders will distort on it. It's also driving loudness to -2.68 LUFS, far past the -9 to -6 LUFS range for this style, and squeezing punch down to 5.5 dB PLR when the genre sits at 6 to 9.5 dB. Dropping the drive addresses the distortion, the loudness and the flatness together.

priorities.title: Low end is lighter than your reference
priorities.why: You're 4.4 dB down below 100 Hz compared to the track you're chasing, at matched volume. For trap that's the weight of the 808s and sub — it'll sound thin next to your reference on systems with real low-end extension.

listen_for: Hair or crackle on the loudest hits and on the transitions — check the file after an MP3/AAC encode, not just the WAV, since the true peak overs show up worst there.
Whether the kick and snare breathe once the limiter gain is down 2–4 dB; A/B at matched volume so the quieter version isn't judged as weaker.
808 and sub weight against your reference on headphones and on a small speaker, looping the loudest section while you set the low shelf.
That the added low shelf doesn't push the limiter back into heavy gain reduction — re-check true peak after the EQ move.
strengths: Stereo image holds together: 0.766 L/R correlation with only 0.56 dB mono loss, so it survives a mono fold-down.
Low end is solid in the middle — 0.785 low-end correlation means the sub isn't fighting itself.
Left/right balance is dead centre at 0.0 dB, and you're at 97% match to your reference across loudness, punch, contrast, tone and width.

judge.priority_order: Critical F1 grouped with F3/F4 leads, correctly placed before the warning-only F2 tone issue.
judge.explains_impact: Priority 1 explains distortion on playback/encoders and squeezed punch; priority 2 explains thinness vs reference on systems with sub extension.
judge.groups_causes: F1, F3, F4 are correctly merged as one limiter-drive cause, while F2 (tone) is kept separate as an unrelated issue.
judge.specific: Notes cite exact figures (+2.8 dBTP, -2.68 LUFS, 5.5 dB PLR, 4.4 dB below 100 Hz, 97% match) tied to this bounce and genre.
judge.stage_appropriate: The report stage is 'master', so loudness should be judged against release standards, but the notes call the file 'clipping hard' and treat loudness as 'the problem' in headline/summary as if it's simply wrong rather than a stage-appropriate release consideration; also true peak over full scale is real but framing conflates limiter drive as strictly bad without noting it's a release-ready master needing peak-safety, not headroom for mastering elsewhere.
judge.faithful: The notes claim the true peak overs 'show up worst' after MP3/AAC encoding as an established fact beyond what the report states (report only says 'expect distortion... after lossy encoding' generically, not a comparative claim), and the headline/summary overstate 'clipping hard' which isn't a term used or clearly supported by the report.
judge.concise: There is redundant repetition of the same three numbers (dBTP, LUFS, PLR) across headline, summary, and priority 'why', padding length without adding new information.
